Nepal’s historic loss and damage allocation falls short of its needs
items.desc: The UN fund has provisionally set aside 21.6 million for Nepal after the Rasuwa disaster, marking a first while covering less than 0.5 percent of the country’s estimated $4.7 billion recovery and reconstruction needs.

items.title: Nepal plans first feasibility study for Himalayan tourism highway
items.desc: The proposed routes would connect Badimalika in the west and Pathibhara in the east, with a six-month study to assess costs, environmental impacts and possible road alignments.

items.title: Activist arrested over protest against Ani Choying Drolma’s appointment
items.desc: Police detained the head of a campaign opposing the appointment of the Buddhist nun as vice-chair of the Lumbini Development Trust after protesters burned a photograph of the tourism minister.

items.title: England forward Kane crowned Ballon d’Or winner, Putellas wins women’s award
items.desc: A 61-goal season for Bayern earns Kane his first Ballon d’Or, 25 years after Michael Owen became the last English winner, while Spain’s Alexia Putellas claims the women’s award for a third time.

items.title: Biratnagar take on Chitwan as Janakpur face Karnali in NPL double-header
items.desc: Andre Russell and Angelo Mathews add star power to Biratnagar, while former champions Janakpur look to bounce back after a disappointing second season.

items.title: In China, the AI bubble has already burst
items.desc: A 40 percent plunge in China’s STAR 50 index has wiped out $480 billion in market value, raising fresh questions about AI valuations and Beijing’s push to steer household savings into stocks.

items.title: Trump approval rises from record low to 32% ahead of midterm election, Reuters Ipsos poll finds
items.desc: Democrats hold an 11-point lead over Republicans in the congressional vote, while concerns over the cost of living weigh on Trump ahead of the November 3 midterms.

items.title: Restore hope for Bhotekoshi flood victims
items.desc: The Bhotekoshi flood victims deserve answers; they cannot remain in uncertainty any longer.

items.title: Devoid of options, flood survivors return to damaged homes
items.desc: The government has announced rent assistance, temporary shelters and new land for resettlement. Survivors and local officials say little of it has reached them.

items.title: She climbed Everest without supplemental oxygen. But the summit was never the point
items.desc: Melissa Arnot Reid, the first American woman to achieve the feat, launched her memoir in Kathmandu, reflecting on shame, self-worth and the people behind Himalayan expeditions.

items.title: After years of delay, Budhigandaki faces another change of plan
items.desc: Successive governments have changed the project’s development models. Latest plan to set up an authority has raised new questions over implementation.

items.title: Oli, Dahal move to extend alliance to next year’s local and provincial polls
items.desc: UML and Nepali Communist Party leaders are exploring grassroots-level electoral cooperation to prevent further erosion of left-wing support.

items.title: Xtreme is betting on Nepali sport. It’s helping both — for now
items.desc: A Nepali energy drink is now sponsoring national cricket team players, seven NPL franchises, and the country’s first franchise volleyball league. But nobody will say how much it is paying.

items.title: Nepal, India to discuss border security at annual meeting this week
items.desc: The three-day talks will focus on cross-border crime, human trafficking, drug smuggling, boundary management and intelligence sharing along the 1,751-kilometre open border.

items.title: Choose your words carefully, minister
items.desc: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle was half right on nationalism and India. But a finance minister abroad speaks for the country, not just his party.

items.title: Nepal seeks talks with Malaysia over recruitment of Nepali workers
items.desc: Kathmandu has proposed a meeting in November or December to discuss Malaysia’s foreign worker recruitment system and renew a labour agreement signed in 2018.

items.title: After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to see how student-backed leaders will govern
items.desc: Tens of thousands took to the streets of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down.

items.title: Lumbini Lions launch title defence with seven-wicket win over Sudurpaschim
items.desc: D’Arcy Short smashes 40 off 18 balls after Kishore Mahato and Sher Malla take seven wickets between them to help the defending champions start NPL season three in style.

items.title: Six killed as Scorpio plunges 250 metres off road in Gulmi
items.desc: Three others were injured when the vehicle travelling from Syangja to Gulmi crashed along the Kaligandaki Corridor road.

items.title: Lumbini bowl out Sudurpaschim for 87 in NPL season opener
items.desc: Kishore Mahato takes four wickets and Sher Malla claims three as defending champions Lumbini Lions dismiss last season’s runners-up in 17.2 overs.

items.title: Why Kathmandu is drinking blind
items.desc: A technique that maps aquifers from the air is changing how countries protect their drinking water. Nepal needs to adopt this method.

items.title: Yasuo Fukuda, Japan’s first second-generation prime minister, dies at 90, Nikkei reports
items.desc: Becoming prime minister on the sudden resignation of Shinzo Abe in 2007, ​Fukuda lasted less than a year — a tenure even shorter than his father Takeo’s two-year stint.

items.title: Nepal Premier League’s third season kicks off with Lumbini bowling first
items.desc: Defending champions Lumbini Lions won the toss and elected to field against Sudurpaschim Royals in the opening match of the eight-team tournament at Kirtipur.

items.title: Tatopani border closure disrupts trade and livelihoods after brief reopening
items.desc: Only 72 cargo containers entered Nepal during a brief reopening. With the crossing shut again, traders face dwindling stocks and local businesses are struggling to survive.

items.title: Most Nepal government websites back online after PHP2Shell flaw
